title: U.S. distance runner, sponsor in dispute over allegation she was dropped after pregnancy
content:
U.S. long-distance runner Emma Bates has alleged she was dropped by a commercial partner after informing them she was pregnant.

Bates, 33, said she lost her sponsorship deal with company UCan, which produces energy gels, bars and powders for endurance athletes. UCan has denied Bates’ version of events and claimed the decision to end the partnership was made before the company had any knowledge of her pregnancy.

A representative of the marathon runner contradicted UCan’s timeline and accused the company of changing its commercial offer to Bates.

“Since my fueling company dropped me after telling them I was pregnant, I have been trying a bunch of new gels,” Bates said in a video posted on Instagram on Tuesday.

Bates, who finished second in the Chicago Marathon in 2021 and fifth in the Boston Marathon in 2023, publicly announced her pregnancy with a post on social media on March 5. She completed the Valencia marathon in 2:25:51 in December, a race she has since confirmed she ran “very early” in her pregnancy.

UCan said the decision to end the partnership was made in September 2025 and that a new proposal was made to Bates, which she did not accept.

“We’re proud of the three-year partnership we had with Emma and the many accomplishments we shared together,” a UCan statement read. “The partnership decisions were made in September 2025 as a part of regular business planning and prior to any knowledge of her pregnancy.

“We made an effort to continue working with Emma under a new agreement, but Emma ultimately chose not to move forward with that option. We’ve always supported and will continue to support athletes at all stages of life, including pregnancy and motherhood. Emma is an incredible athlete and we sincerely wish her the very best.”

Matt Sonnenfeldt of the Flynn Sports Management, the agency which represents Bates, denied UCan’s version of events and told Front Office Sports: “We were in discussions after September. They made an offer in December and then changed it.” The Athletic has contacted FSM for comment.

In August 2019, Nike announced a new maternity policy for its athletes after six-time Olympic champion Alysson Felix, 800m bronze medalist Alysia Montano and 10,000m world silver medalist Kara Goucher told the New York Times that their sponsorship payments had been reduced, or attempted to be renegotiated at a lower rate, by the sportswear giant while they were pregnant.
